# Pandamonium v1.0.72

Entertainment is now a native, owner-scoped Pandamonium surface backed by the complete pinned AniCLI and PandaFlix upstream applications. The release adds real search, browsing, playback, and history flows without exposing either CLI to chat or voice. Rollback is signed v1.0.71 with the updater snapshot.

## MAD-972 — Entertainment: integrate AniCLI and PandaFlix end to end

### Problem

The Marketplace packages were reduced demonstrations rather than complete upstream applications, and Settings had no native way to use their real media workflows. That left discovery disconnected from search, episode selection, stream resolution, subtitles, and playback.

### Implementation

AniCLI 5.1.2 and PandaFlix 1.2.1 now install their pinned complete upstream sources and dependencies inside the existing bounded private package runtime. Strict provider contracts expose only the declared Entertainment operations. Settings conditionally hides Entertainment, opens a single installed provider directly, or shows a fullscreen Anime / Movies & Shows chooser when both are installed.

The native player uses direct HTTPS streams first. A bounded, owner-scoped proxy is available only when upstream headers or cookies are required, with public-address validation, pinned transport, redirect, playlist, range, token-expiry, and response-size limits. Media providers remain unavailable to chat, agent tools, and voice.

### Product value and UI visibility

Anime supports real sub/dub search, episode selection, quality, playback, and upstream history/continue behavior. Movies & Shows supports real title search, movie playback, series seasons and episodes. Resolved streams and subtitles play in the fullscreen HTML5 player, with HLS support provided by the bundled Apache-2.0 hls.js asset.

### Verification

Protected CI passed the full Python suite, the full Chromium browser suite, syntax, secret, workflow, dependency, container, and image gates. Focused Entertainment coverage passed 12 Python checks and its Chromium flow. Disposable live-source proof resolved an AniCLI episode, a PandaFlix movie, and a PandaFlix series episode with subtitles and required request headers.

Both packages were validated in the kernel-bounded runtime before immutable publication. Live signed-catalog readback confirms AniCLI 5.1.2 at `2a956db02bf83760bf8f28b720d58fe8014b0e9b` and PandaFlix 1.2.1 at `f6484787ba5a23d4453d5bbd8eb34f05054ecfbb`, with their published artifact hashes.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No database schema, environment variable, host dependency, authentication, or voice integration changed. Packages retain GPL upstream attribution; bundled hls.js retains Apache-2.0 attribution. This publication proves source, immutable package, and signed Marketplace availability. Operator-visible acceptance through a later normal Marketplace install remains intentionally separate. No CT103 installation, deployment, or runtime mutation was performed.
